text:
ryan: opening a short thread on a feedback-driven pack-window idea. problem: static router pack windows either underpack (wasted latency) or overpack (KV miss & cost spikes). looking for a low-risk handshake with runtime to adapt pack_window_ms per-shard.
tess: interesting. what's the runtime signal surface you want?
ryan: proposal: runtime emits a compact headroom & eviction summary in enqueue responses: `{headroom_ms: int, eviction_rate_ppm: int, kv_miss_trend: int8}`. router uses this to adjust pack window with a PID-ish controller.
anika: i'm worried about oscillation and cross-shard ripple. tuning PID across thousands of shards is hard. how do we prevent coordinated oscillations?
ryan: plan: per-shard smoothing with a bounded clamp and a cluster-wide dampener: if >10% shards change window by >X concurrently we apply exponential backoff. plus a small randomized jitter to updates.
mo: behavior on DEFER/REJECT from runtime? if runtime rejects a packed envelope because headroom changed, router should split and re-enqueue per-item, not drop. also emit a rate-limited signal so router learns.
ryan: yes. runtime responses: OK, SUGGEST_WINDOW_MS, or REJECT_DEFER. SUGGEST_WINDOW_MS is important 1 we can converge faster when runtime is under pressure.
tess: we need metrics. add `router.applied_pack_window_ms`, `runtime.suggested_pack_window_ms`, `runtime.eviction_rate_ppm`, `router.split_rate_on_reject`. also tracepack id to map packed envelopes.
anika: fairness: how do you prevent pack window increases for a shard with many small requests from starving other tenants on the same GPU?
ryan: two layers: router enforces per-tenant soft quotas before cross-tenant packing; runtime still does final admission per-item inside the envelope. if runtime indicates that a tenant is causing high eviction_rate, router reduces that tenant's eligible fraction for cross-tenant packs.
mo: implementation note: keep the runtime-to-router payload tiny (1-2 ints) to avoid adding latency. and make it opt-in per-deployment.
tess: rollout: 5% canary regionally, watch 30m sliding windows. auto-degrade rule: if p99 latency increases >7% or kv_miss_rate absolute delta >2%. also add cost regression guard: tokens/req p95 > +8% rollback.
anika: debugability: we must be able to reconstruct original item latencies from packed envelopes. add sampled unpack mapping (`router.unpack_sample_rate`) and emit a lightweight index digest in logs.yan: sample config snippet i'm prototyping:
```yaml
feedback_pack:
  enabled: true
  min_window_ms: 2
  max_window_ms: 30
  initial_window_ms: 6
  smoothing_alpha: 0.15
  cluster_dampener_threshold: 0.1
  cluster_dampener_backoff_ms: 1000
  per_tenant_soft_quota: 500
  small_bypass_tokens: 10
  unpack_sample_rate: 1/1000
```
mo: +1 for having an explicit controller. we should also simulate with a traffic generator that injects hot-tenant spikes and long-seq mixes before canary.
tess: agree. add an eval set with repeated-prefix long-docs to catch warmup regressions.
anika: one more: keep runtime API backward compatible. router should degrade gracefully if runtime doesn't understand suggested fields.
infra-bot: deploybot: scheduled canary for infra-canary-15 in 20m. streaming metrics: router.applied_pack_window_ms, runtime.eviction_rate_ppm, runtime.kv_miss_rate, p99_latency. auto-rollback enabled.yan: i'll open the PR with controller impl + sim results and add dashboards. action items: Ryan = PR + sim; Tess = canary guard queries; Anika = fairness stress scenarios; Mo = runtime tiny-response impl. thanks everyone.
